1/ Why one shielded transfer isn't enough

Mixers and one-off shields break the link once. Then you spend from a normal wallet and the trail stitches itself back together.

Anyone can open this.

2/ Balance on your screen. Not on the explorer.

One account. Your shielded balance, and a card that draws from it directly. Nothing about it has to be published to be spendable.

3/ You program the swipe

Dinner paid. 10 STRK moved where you told it to. One transaction, one signature.

This is the part nobody else does: the rule fires inside the payment, not after it.

4/ Prove the $84 dinner. Not the rest of the account.

When someone needs proof a payment happened, a viewing key generates a statement for that single authorization and exposes nothing else.

5/ How to try it, 3 steps

1. Connect @ready_co (it holds the viewing key on your device)
2. Get Sepolia STRK from a faucet
3. Shield, then swipe

Takes about 5 minutes. sealed.cash

6/ Where this actually stands

Everything above is @Starknet Sepolia. Real transactions, test money. The card is Lithic's issuer sandbox, not a live program.

On mainnet we've shielded real STRK into the canonical STRK20 pool, Accepted on L1. Sealed itself isn't on mainnet yet.

If you break it, reply with the hash. I'll look at every one tonight.
